## 1. Precise theorem

Let P be a fixed parameter-free interpretation program with finite control. Its input vocabulary has arity at most two; its finitely many state vocabularies are arbitrary fixed relational vocabularies. Every interpretation has dimension between one and a fixed K. All defining formulas, transition tests, halt tests and output tests are FO with the ordinary, one-variable-on-each-side Härtig quantifier.

Use the following quotient convention, which is the convention of the prior explicit-model candidate: the equality formula generates its least equivalence closure on the interpreted domain, and output relations have existential-representative semantics. Standard interpretations with an already-definable equivalence relation and congruent output relations are special cases.

Put

    r = max(2, all arities appearing in P),
    S = max(size of the original input, sizes of all source states).

There are a fixed binary-vocabulary, parameter-free two-dimensional interpretation program Q and a constant C_P such that:

1. On every input A with |A| at least two, Q simulates P, including its halt/output behavior. If P does not halt, neither does Q.
2. Each source transition is simulated by a bounded number of target transitions, with the bound depending only on P, under the specified quotient convention.
3. Every target state in a simulation of a finite source run has at most

       C_P (1 + S)^(K r)

   vertices. This bound does not involve the runtime or prior discarded states.
4. At each simulation boundary the target is a fresh canonical incidence representation of the current source state, plus a fixed finite set of markers and finite-control flags.
5. All formulas of Q have fixed finite width independent of the runtime and of S.

The same construction can be used in a target formalism requiring equivalence/congruence rather than automatic equivalence closure and existential relations. Section 8 adds a finite FO closure loop. Its runtime need not be constant per simulated transition, but the same state-space bound holds.

The exponent K r is a convenient uniform upper bound, not an optimization. Constants absorb the number of symbols, coordinates, phases and markers.

## 2. What the primary literature says, and what is supplied here

GKPS15 defines FO+H and interpretation programs in §III. Its Remark 2 observes binary-vocabulary sufficiency.

# History-independent dimension and binary-vocabulary compiler

Audit and explicit construction, 2026-10-08.

## Verdict

**The quantitative compiler is proved for programs on binary relational inputs of size at least two, with arbitrary fixed relational intermediate vocabularies and arbitrary fixed interpretation dimensions.** It also applies when an arbitrary-vocabulary input has already been supplied in the binary incidence representation defined below. Every simulated source state is represented canonically, with precisely one distinguished vertex per logical element. The maximum target universe is polynomial in the maximum source universe, independently of the number of simulated steps.

There is an important scope qualification. If an unencoded input has arbitrary high arity, and the very first output must already be binary and have a two-dimensional universe, one cannot in general construct a lossless representation of that input. For arity at least five this follows from an elementary information bound. Thus do not combine the separate dimension-reduction and vocabulary-reduction observations without checking initialization. The positive binary-input result is sufficient for the proposed exponential lower bound, whose input vocabulary is already binary.

Here “binary vocabulary” means a fixed finite vocabulary whose relation symbols have arity at most two. Unary predicates and finite-control flags can instead be represented using additional binary diagonal predicates, so the final vocabulary may have every symbol of arity exactly two. No claim that the final vocabulary consists of a *single* binary symbol is needed or proved here.

# Independent audit of the history-independent HF simulation

Date: 2026-10-08.

## Verdict

**No fatal flaw found. The stated simulation theorem is valid with its explicit scope.** A fixed GKPS/Rossman HF term program on unary/binary finite input, with at least two input atoms, admits one fixed parameter-free FO+unary-Härtig interpretation simulation whose maximum universe is polynomial in the maximum inclusive hereditary size of the native states plus the input size. The polynomial is independent of the number of native iterations. The companion resettable binary/two-dimensional compiler preserves this conclusion.

This is an independent mathematical audit, supplemented by exact finite tests. It is not a machine-checked formal proof, and it does not independently establish the lower-bound theorem to which the simulation might be applied.

I recorded `BLIND_RECONSTRUCTION.md` before opening the proposed proof. The blind argument independently found the semantic-footprint, canonical-quotient, on-demand-counting, and garbage-collection route. It used a more general iterative extensional-equality mechanism; the submitted proof's one-layer constructor is simpler and sufficient.

Primary source: [Grädel, Kaiser, Pakusa, Schalthöfer, Characterising Choiceless Polynomial Time with First-Order Interpretations, LICS 2015](https://www.logic.rwth-aachen.de/pub/schalthoefer/GKPS15.pdf).
